sections.title: What is LIC Single Premium Endowment Plan (917/717/817)?

content.text: The LIC Single Premium Endowment Plan (Plan No. 917) is a straightforward savings-cum-protection plan where you pay the premium only once at the start of the policy. It's a hassle-free, one-time investment that provides a combination of guaranteed savings and life insurance coverage. At the end of the policy term, you receive a lump sum maturity amount, and your family is protected with a death benefit throughout the term. It's an ideal solution for those who have a lump sum amount and want to secure it for a future goal.

items: Riders: Accidental Death & Disability Benefit Rider and a New Term Assurance Rider are available.
Tax Benefits: Premium paid can be claimed under Section 80C. Maturity is tax-free under 10(10D) if the Sum Assured is at least 10 times the premium.

sections.title: Benefits vs. Drawbacks of This Plan

rows: Returns are modest and may not beat high inflation.
Guaranteed lump sum maturity plus life cover.
Requires a large upfront premium payment.
Maturity may become taxable if Sum Assured is less than 10x the premium.
Loan and surrender facility available for liquidity.
Liquidity is low in the early years of the policy.
Safe, guaranteed returns (typically 5-6% IRR), often higher than FDs post-tax.
Not a high-growth instrument like equity mutual funds.

content.text: This plan is not for everyone, but it's an excellent fit for specific profiles:

items: Risk-Averse Investors: Individuals who prioritize capital safety over high returns.
Those with Lump Sum Funds: Perfect for retirees with a corpus, people who received a bonus, or NRIs looking to invest a one-time amount in India.
Goal-Based Planners: Parents or grandparents planning for a child's future education or marriage with a fixed, one-time investment.

sections.title: LIC Single Premium Endowment vs. Other Investments

items.q: What is an LIC Single Premium Endowment Plan maturity calculator?
items.a: It's a tool that estimates the final lump sum you'll receive at the end of your policy term. It adds your Sum Assured to the estimated vested bonuses and a potential Final Additional Bonus (FAB) to give you a clear projection.

items.q: What is the return on LIC Single Premium Endowment Plan?
items.a: The plan typically offers an illustrative Internal Rate of Return (IRR) between 5% to 6%, depending on the term and age. While modest, this return is generally tax-free, making it competitive with post-tax FD returns.
The maturity amount is tax-free under Section 10(10D) *if* the Sum Assured is at least 10 times the single premium paid. If not, the entire maturity amount becomes taxable.

items.q: Can I take a loan on this plan?
items.a: Yes, a loan facility is available after the completion of one policy year. This provides a good liquidity option without having to surrender the policy.

items.q: What is the surrender value of LIC single premium plan?
items.a: The policy acquires a surrender value immediately after premium payment. You can surrender it anytime. The Guaranteed Surrender Value is 75% of the Single Premium in the first year, and 90% thereafter. A Special Surrender Value, which is usually higher, may also be payable.

items.q: Which is better: LIC single premium vs FD vs PPF?
items.a: It depends on your goal. Choose LIC for a combined insurance + savings goal with a one-time investment. Choose FD for short-term goals with high liquidity. Choose PPF for long-term, tax-free wealth creation with recurring investments.

items.q: Is LIC Single Premium Endowment Plan good or bad?
items.a: It's 'good' for risk-averse individuals who need a safe, one-time investment with an insurance component. It's 'bad' for investors seeking high, inflation-beating returns, for whom equity mutual funds would be a better choice.
